default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-468.title: Seasonal-path deviation fade
E-468.hypothesis: Against the typical same-minute path of the day-return over 20 sessions, a day running far from it is stretched versus what intraday flow usually does; fade it.

E-469.title: Negative-autocorrelation regime fade
E-469.hypothesis: When the rolling lag-1 return autocorrelation is clearly negative, bar moves are bid-ask bounce and liquidity-taker overshoots; a large bar is faded by market makers.

E-470.title: One-sided bar-colour fraction fade
E-470.hypothesis: When almost all recent bars close one colour, aggressive flow is crowded on one side and the marginal buyer or seller is spent; fade the first time the fraction reaches the level.

E-471.title: Bollinger band re-entry
E-471.hypothesis: A close outside a rolling mean +/- m sigma band followed by a close back inside shows the push was absorbed; fade back toward the mean.

E-472.title: Volatility expansion direction follow
E-472.hypothesis: When the short-window average range jumps well above the hour's average, new information is being priced in; follow the direction of the short window.

E-473.title: EMA stretch in range units fade
E-473.hypothesis: A close far from its own EMA, measured in average bar ranges, is an inventory-driven stretch that mean-reverts as liquidity providers lean against it.

E-474.title: Rolling-VWAP cross on heavy volume
E-474.hypothesis: A close across the trailing-hour volume-weighted price on heavier than usual volume marks a shift in the cost basis of recent participants; follow it.

E-475.title: Wide-window Donchian midline cross
E-475.hypothesis: In a window wider than usual, a close crossing the high-low midpoint shows the balance point migrating; follow it.

E-476.title: Prior-session midpoint reclaim
E-476.hypothesis: The midpoint of yesterday's range is a fair-value reference for today's participants; after trading on one side for a while, the first close across it hands control to the other side.

E-477.title: Seasonal minute-of-day forward drift
E-477.hypothesis: If over the last 20 sessions the forward return from this minute has had a consistent sign (net drift close to its average absolute size), recurring flow (rebalancing, hedging) may repeat; trade it.
